articleTitle: Visualization Analysis of Artificial Intelligence Applications in Rural Areas Based on Citespace
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Conference on Information Science, Parallel and Distributed Systems (ISPDS)
abstract: With the rapid development of artificial intelligence, research on its application in rural development is increasing. This paper focuses on the literature on artificial intelligence empowering rural and agricultural development from the Web of Science core from 2014 to 2023. Using CiteSpace software, it conducts a visualization analysis of the literature over the past decade, examining the current status, hotpots, and trends of research from six aspects: publication quantity, disciplinary distribution, institutions, countries and regions distribution, research hotpots, and trends. Conclusion: Regarding the current status, there is rich international research on the application of artificial intelligence in rural areas, with an overall increasing trend in research quantity since 2018. Collaboration networks among institutions have begun to form, with China, the United States, and India conducting more research with higher impact. Regarding research hotpots, machine learning and deep learning are popular application technologies, with digital agriculture and precision agriculture being the main research objects over the past decade. Regarding research trends, integrating artificial intelligence technology with smart rural development and smart agriculture will further deepen.

articleTitle: Implementation of FIR Digital Filter Algorithm in C Language on DSP Platform
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Conference on Information Science, Parallel and Distributed Systems (ISPDS)
abstract: This article provides a detailed overview of the process of implementing an FIR digital filter using the TI TMS320 series DSP platform with the C programming language. It covers topics such as the working principle of FIR filters, design methods, DSP development environment setup, C code implementation, simulation verification, and system testing. Through simulation verification, the frequency response characteristics of the FIR filter are confirmed, and the system testing results demonstrate that the FIR filter achieves effective signal filtering under appropriate conditions with accurate frequency response and high signal-to-noise ratio. This document comprehensively validates the excellent signal processing performance of FIR filters on the DSP platform, offering valuable insights for applications involving FIR filter design on DSP platforms.

articleTitle: A Book Recommendation Algorithm for High Vocational School Library Based on Deep Learning
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Conference on Information Science, Parallel and Distributed Systems (ISPDS)
abstract: Aiming at the many shortcomings of collaborative filtering algorithms in traditional recommender systems, such as cold-start and data sparsity, a book recommendation algorithm based on deep learning is proposed. Firstly, multiple data sources are fused to collect readers' information and books' information to enrich readers' side features and books' side features; then the deep learning model is utilized to extract readers' embedding features and books' embedding features; then the dot product of the two is used as the output, which is used as the basis for providing recommendations to users; finally, this paper conducts experiments by comparing with the ALS algorithm. The experimental results show that the model proposed in this paper improves the data sparsity and cold-start problems, and improves the book recommendation efficiency.

articleTitle: Research on Automated Construction and Extraction Methods for Automotive Information Security Test Cases Based on Knowledge Graphs
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Conference on Information Science, Parallel and Distributed Systems (ISPDS)
abstract: As automotive information security is increasingly emphasized, the demand for automotive information security testing by car companies is increasing. In order to improve the efficiency of test case generation, as well as to better organize and extract the increasing number of test cases, this paper proposes a method for constructing and extracting automotive information security test cases. The method improves the data storage efficiency of test cases with large data volume and the extraction efficiency of test case execution steps by constructing a test case knowledge graph, coding atomic operations using encoding, and constructing a test case execution path.

articleTitle: A Safe Transfer Learning Approach Inspired by Desensitization Therapy
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Conference on Information Science, Parallel and Distributed Systems (ISPDS)
abstract: Transfer learning is a mainstream method to solve data scarcity tasks, but it faces the threat of defect inheritance, which makes the student model vulnerable to adversarial example attacks. Traditional solutions include model slicing and model reconstruction. However, due to the uninterpretability of deep neural networks, model slicing methods often adopt a conservative way, which leads to the limited resistance of the model to adversarial example attacks. Inspired by the theory of the biomedical field, this paper proposes a node optimization method based on desensitization therapy (STL-DMP). In STL-DMP, the student model is regarded as an allergic person, the abnormal state of the student model after being attacked by the adversarial sample is regarded as an allergic reaction, the interference is regarded as an allergen, model weights are regarded as sensitizing-cell activity mediators, and the loss function is regarded as an immune regulatory signal. Based on the above statement, STL-DMP uses interference (allergens) to prepare adversarial samples (vaccines). The student model (allergy) is exposed to a specific perturbation (allergen) by training (treatment) with dedicated adversarial examples (vaccines). The model weights (sensitizing-cell activity mediators) are gradually weakened (consumed to an equilibrium value), thus eliminating the threat of adversarial sample attacks (sensitized state). Experiments show that STL-DMP improves the resistance of the model to adversarial attacks while maintaining accuracy.

articleTitle: Early Detection and Intervention of Alzheimer's disease Based on Game APP
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Conference on Information Science, Parallel and Distributed Systems (ISPDS)
abstract: In terms of the increasing prevalence of Alzheimer's disease (AD) with aging, this paper designed a Chinese version of Game APP based on the fusion of MOCA and MMSE, and the correlation analysis of the scores of the 10 tasks of 64 subjects proved the rationality of the game design. The combination of significance, T-test and correlation coefficient method reveals the common trend of brain cognition degradation with age. This work helps to promote the detection and intervention at the early stage of AD, which is worthy of in-depth study.

articleTitle: Accountable Attribute-Based Matching Encryption for The Internet of Vehicles
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Conference on Information Science, Parallel and Distributed Systems (ISPDS)
abstract: Due to the openness of communication methods in the Internet of Vehicles (IoV), its data transmission is vulnerable to attacks. Additionally, a vast amount of redundant data saturates the IoV's data space. How to ensure the security of transmitted information while achieving efficient data source identification is an important challenge facing the development of the IoV industry. Matching encryption technology holds promising research prospects for achieving data security and data source access control. This paper proposes an accountable attribute-based matching encryption for the IoV, addressing the lack of effective user tracking, revocation, and privacy protection mechanisms in existing attribute-based matching encryption techniques for practical scenarios of IoV data sharing. The scheme implements functionalities such as revocation, white-box tracking, and user privacy protection. We analyze the confidentiality, authenticity, and traceability of this scheme under a random oracle model. Additionally, performance analysis is conducted to demonstrate its practicality in real-world scenarios.

articleTitle: Industrial 5G Private Network Deterministic Technology Research and Verification
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Conference on Information Science, Parallel and Distributed Systems (ISPDS)
abstract: As the demand for industrial automation increases, the application of 5G technology in the industrial field is coming into focus. In particular, 5G's ultra-reliable low-latency communication (URLLC) and time-sensitive network (TSN) technologies are seen as the key to realizing efficient industrial communication. Despite the continuous progress in theoretical research and standardization, experimental data and application research in real environments are still relatively insufficient, which limits the verification of theoretical results for practical applications. In this paper, we present a detailed description of 5G deterministic communication technology in industrial environments, and design experiments to verify the effectiveness of 5G TSN gating function and its impact on service flow under different priority settings. This paper aims to fill the gap in existing research on experimental data. The experimental results show that the configuration of priority and gating significantly reduces the delay and packet loss rate, confirming the effectiveness and reliability of 5G TSN technology in real industrial applications. These findings further validate the critical role of 5G technologies in supporting Industry 4.0 and provide strong evidence for future industrial network design and optimization.

articleTitle: An Adaptive Information Presentation Method Based on Knowledge Graph and Context
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Conference on Information Science, Parallel and Distributed Systems (ISPDS)
abstract: This paper presents an adaptive information presentation system and method based on knowledge graphs and context within the realm of adaptive information presentation technology. The method utilizes natural language processing technology to analyze the user's input question in order to extract the semantic and key information. As users query specific keywords or topics repeatedly, the method processes the responses considering the user's context to deliver more precise information that aligns with the user's information requirements. With an increase in the frequency of user queries, the user's question history is organized into multiple sessions, offering personalized answers based on the user's inquiries within the session. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed method achieves a balance between universality and personalized service in question-answering systems, ensuring problem-solving continuity and enhancing user satisfaction.

articleTitle: An Iot Trust Analysis Method for Frequency Modulation Transactions of West-to-East Power Transmission Units
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Conference on Information Science, Parallel and Distributed Systems (ISPDS)
abstract: This paper overcomes the shortcomings of the existing technology, and proposes a trust calculation method of Internet of things for frequency modulation transactions of West Power to East power transmission units. The basic principle is as follows: Considering the data information formed by data transmission rate and data storage and sharing, and the data error and missing formed by data collection, the iot trust degree for frequency modulation transaction of West-East Power transmission unit is calculated by using the sufficient amount and missing amount of information, and the influence of trust degree on frequency modulation transaction of West-East power transmission unit is evaluated.

articleTitle: Research on Lightweight Obstacle Detection Model Based on Improved YOLOv5s
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Conference on Information Science, Parallel and Distributed Systems (ISPDS)
abstract: The paper intends to investigate the accuracy and lightweight by improving the YOLOv5s model to enhance the sensing ability of campus AGVs on eight types of dynamic obstacles, and effectively solve the problem that it is difficult to balance the real-time and accuracy of its target detection. On the basis of YOLOv5s model, GhostConv is introduced to replace the ordinary convolution, which reduces the number of parameters and computation of the model without affecting the detection accuracy, and at the same time, it adopts the weighted bidirectional feature pyramid BiFPN and the edge regression loss function EIoU to obtain the feature maps with richer feature information, which improves the model generalization ability and detection performance. The results show that the improved model significantly reduces the number of parameters and computation of the model with little effect on the mean average precision mAP, which decreases by 16% and 13%, respectively, compared with the YOLOv5s model, while the inference speed is also improved by 28%, realizing the balance between lightweight and detection accuracy, and the obtained lightweight network model is useful for the embedded devices with weak computational capability is more friendly.

articleTitle: A TCAM-based String Matching Algorithm for Network Intrusion Detection System
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Conference on Information Science, Parallel and Distributed Systems (ISPDS)
abstract: String matching plays an important role in Network Intrusion Detection System(NIDS), including functions like URL filtering and protocol recognition, etc.. This paper proposes a high-speed string matching algorithm based on TCAM to implement fixed-offset and float-offset matching at the same time. Floating-offset strings are stored in TCAM at byte-by-byte offsets, occupying multiple TCAM entries; fixed-offset strings use quotient and residual values of offsets divided by skip distance to represent the matching position, occupying only a single TCAM entry. The input text is segmented and then sent to the TCAM for matching along with current skip count. Both floating-offset strings and fixed-offset strings can be matched in a single pass. This matching algorithm was implemented using NPS-400 network processor and NLA122048 TCAM, which can achieve a matching performance of 100Gbps under a scale of 10K string patterns in NIDS system.

articleTitle: Anomaly Monitoring of Hydropower Units under Complex Conditions
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Conference on Information Science, Parallel and Distributed Systems (ISPDS)
abstract: Hydropower has now become a fundamental industry and infrastructure for the social and economic development of our country. While hydropower brings convenience and benefits, it also comes with significant safety hazards. Therefore, real-time condition monitoring of hydropower units is necessary. This paper addressed the complex operational conditions of hydropower units by first dividing the data into mixed datasets containing both normal and abnormal data, and independent datasets where normal and abnormal data were separated. For the mixed datasets with both normal and abnormal data, the upper and lower bounds for anomaly detection were obtained using the standard deviation criterion based on normalized weighting and Monte Carlo simulation. For the independent datasets that follow a normal distribution, the dynamic upper and lower bounds for anomaly detection were determined based on the standard deviation criterion. For the independent datasets that do not follow a normal distribution, anomaly monitoring and calculation were performed based on multi-factor indicators. Experimental results show that when the proposed methods were applied to actual data from hydropower units under complex conditions, the accuracy of anomaly detection was relatively high, resulting in better monitoring of abnormal conditions.

articleTitle: Design of Transcranial Pulse Electrical Stimulator Based on Virtual Instrumentation
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Conference on Information Science, Parallel and Distributed Systems (ISPDS)
abstract: Transcranial electrical stimulation is a non-invasive neuromodulation technique that affects the brain's activity patterns by stimulating specific areas of the cerebral cortex with low-intensity electrical currents that modulate neuronal excitability and synaptic transmission<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">[1]</sup>. Traditional transcranial stimulation instruments are expensive, bulky and have poor portability. In this paper, a new type of portable transcranial instrument is developed, using LabVIEW to develop the upper computer system, the output electrical stimulation parameters are controlled by the upper computer, and the lower computer uses the STM32 microcontroller with low power consumption as the main control chip, and the upper computer software displays the parameter information during operation. The experiments show that the instrument is characterized by strong controllability, high portability and stability, and has high practical value.

articleTitle: Effect of the Substrate Heat Conduction on the Heat Distribution Type MEMS Natural Gas Flow Sensor
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Conference on Information Science, Parallel and Distributed Systems (ISPDS)
abstract: The MEMS gas flow sensor produced by the combination of the MEMS technology and the sensor technology has gradually become a research hotspot in the field of gas flow detection. The heat distribution type gas flow sensor based on the MEMS technology can be used to detect the natural gas flow by using the principle that the natural gas flow will take away part of the heat when passing through the detection area, resulting in a temperature difference between the upstream and the downstream of the heating resistor. The solid heat conduction between the resistors and the substrate absorbs some of the heat, which will affect the detection accuracy of the sensor. In this paper, the effects of the substrate heat conduction on the temperature field distribution, fluid velocity field distribution, and the temperature difference between the upstream and the downstream of the heating resistor in the detection area are discussed by simulation research. The results show that the substrate heat conduction has a great effect on the temperature field distribution, but has little effect on the velocity field distribution. At the same time, the substrate heat conduction has a great influence on the temperature difference between the upstream and the downstream of the heating resistor. Without heat insulation measures, the temperature difference between the upstream and the downstream decreased significantly, with an average decrease rate as high as 28.8%.

articleTitle: Models Based on Dynamics and Discrete Global Optimisation Algorithms
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Conference on Information Science, Parallel and Distributed Systems (ISPDS)
abstract: This paper provides a comprehensive investigation into computational models based on dynamics and discrete global optimization algorithms. It explores the theoretical foundations and practical applications of these models in diverse computational contexts. Through a detailed analysis of existing literature and empirical studies, the paper examines the principles and methodologies underlying dynamic systems and discrete optimization techniques. Furthermore, it explores the implementation of these algorithms in various computational problems, highlighting their effectiveness in solving complex optimization tasks. The study presents case studies and empirical results demonstrating the performance and applicability of these models across different domains. By bridging theoretical concepts with practical applications, this research contributes to advancing computational methodologies, offering valuable insights for researchers and practitioners in the field of computer science and optimization.

articleTitle: Prediction of Subgrade Settlement of High-speed Railway Based on BP Neural Network Optimized by Crested Porcupine
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Conference on Information Science, Parallel and Distributed Systems (ISPDS)
abstract: In order to predict the settlement of high-speed railway embankment more accurately, a BP neural network model optimized by crested porcupine algorithm (CPO) is proposed, aiming at the fact that the traditional BP neural network is simple to sink into local optimum and over-fitting. The crested porcupine optimization algorithm mainly uses the four defense behaviours of the crested porcupine, namely vision, sound, smell and body attack, to obtain the optimal solution, so as to obtain the optimal weight and threshold of the BP neural network to predict the settlement of the high-speed rail roadbed. The monitoring data were inputted into the traditional BP model and CPO-BP model for training and prediction, and the models were evaluated by MAE, RMSE, MAPE, R<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> evaluation indicators. In comparison to the traditional BP neural network model, the errors of CPO-BP model were reduced by 67.9%, 63.64%, 42.86%, respectively, and the fitting coefficient was improved from 96.62% to 99.55%. The model has high prediction accuracy and provides a new method for high-speed railway subgrade settlement prediction.

articleTitle: Infant Speech Emotion Recognition Based on Channel Attention Mechanism with ResNet-BiLSTM
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Conference on Information Science, Parallel and Distributed Systems (ISPDS)
abstract: Infants communicate their emotional needs through speech, which contains rich emotional information. In view of the fact that there is no publicly available infant speech emotion data set and the accuracy of existing infant speech emotion recognition methods is poor, in this paper, we collected 6100 infant speech samples from the Internet through crawling and other methods as the infant speech emotion recognition data set, and proposed a ResNet-BiLSTM model integrating channel attention mechanism for infant speech emotion recognition. The model first uses MFCC with dynamic and static feature fusion as input, then uses ResNet network embedded in SENet module to extract channel information of input features, and then sends it to BiLSTM model to extract speech context information. Finally, a fully connected layer is used for classification to obtain the final recognition result. The experimental results show that the proposed method can achieve an accuracy of 85% on the infant speech emotion dataset, which is 9% higher than the ordinary ResNet.

articleTitle: A Emergency Path Planning Method for UAV Based on A-star Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Conference on Information Science, Parallel and Distributed Systems (ISPDS)
abstract: This article proposes a UAV emergency path planning technology based on the A * algorithm for power application scenarios, taking into account parameters such as inspection efficiency and safety boundaries, thereby improving the overall safety and efficiency of drone operations. The testing algorithm has been experimentally validated and achieved good results under constraints in 2D, 3D and other dynamic changing scenarios with multiple drones undergoing.

articleTitle: Health-Aware Contrastive Learning for Recipe Recommendation
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Conference on Information Science, Parallel and Distributed Systems (ISPDS)
abstract: This paper addresses the shortcomings of traditional recipe recommendation systems, which often neglect nutritional balance and health needs, while facing challenges such as long-tail effects and data noise. We propose the "Health-Aware Contrastive Learning for Recipe Recommendation" (HACL) model. HACL constructs a nutritional assessment framework to align with users' health requirements and incorporates contrastive learning strategies to address the long-tail distribution and noise in knowledge graphs (KG). By building local and non-local knowledge graphs and implementing multi-level contrastive learning, HACL effectively extracts intrinsic graph information and optimizes long-tail and noise issues. Additionally, the model integrates contrastive loss for health attributes during the learning process, emphasizing the importance of health factors and enhancing the health orientation of recommendations. Experimental validation on two real recipe datasets demonstrates the effectiveness and superiority of HACL.

articleTitle: A fast Electromagnetic Scattering Computation Method for Multiple Hybrid Targets
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Conference on Information Science, Parallel and Distributed Systems (ISPDS)
abstract: In modern local warfare, targets are often hybrid and grouped, so it is of great significance to investigate the electromagnetic scattering characteristics of multiple hybrid targets. In this paper, the hybrid dielectric and conductor target is analysed using both induced electric and magnetic currents in iterative calculations, with the introduction of the energy change rate. This enables the iterative calculations to be stopped when the change rate is lower than a set threshold value. In the case of multiple targets that do not satisfy the far-field conditions, the physical optics (PO) method is enhanced to render it suitable for near-area coupled scattering solving calculations. This is achieved by establishing a local coordinate system around the source point on the target surface and expanding the origin of the local coordinate system as the expansion point of the source point for the level expansion. The Green's function is then corrected, and the solution calculations for the integral equation of the scattering field are ultimately realised. Furthermore, in order to accelerate the computation, FaFFA is introduced in this paper, which reduces the computational complexity and memory consumption. The numerical results demonstrate a high degree of concordance between the results obtained through the near-field iterative PO method and those produced by the MLFMM solver in the commercial software FEKO.

articleTitle: A Digital Currency Scheme Based on Blind Signatures Using Chaotic Hash Functions and RSA Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Conference on Information Science, Parallel and Distributed Systems (ISPDS)
abstract: Blind signature is a cryptographic technique where a signer signs a message without knowing its content, thereby protecting the privacy of the message. It is widely used in digital currencies, electronic voting systems, anonymous credentials, and other areas. In response to the shortcomings of some existing blind signature schemes in terms of security and efficiency, this article proposes a digital currency scheme based on chaotic hash function and RSA algorithm blind signatures. The chaotic hash function is used to convert digital currencies, improving the shortcomings of previous algorithms. The proposed scheme has anonymous and non-traceable characteristics, can resist various attacks, and has a relatively short processing time, with higher computational efficiency and security performance.

articleTitle: Research on Performance Analysis Techniques for Parallel Program Optimization on Domestic CPU Architecture
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Conference on Information Science, Parallel and Distributed Systems (ISPDS)
abstract: With the increasing use of high-performance computing, users are turning to programs for concurrent execution enhance the speed and overall performance of large-scale programs. This trend is supported through the use of a portable messaging interface (MPI), communication can be facilitated in a convenient and efficient manner. We employ the MPI-based performance analysis tool mpiP for evaluating program performance, focusing on a matrix multiplication model through numerous targeted experiments with a fixed number of processors. Expanding the scale of the experimental use case matrix; fixing the scale of the matrix and scaling up the number of processors in order to clearly analyze the program performance and improve the performance analysis of mpiP. At the same time, the execution sequence detection and visualization functions are added in the improvement process. The mpiP report makes it easier for users to perform global performance analysis on the program. This not only improves the overall performance analysis efficiency, it also facilitates tracking the progress of individual processes throughout the program's execution.

articleTitle: PFIDT:Pyramid Focal Inverse Distance Transformer for Crowd Localization
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Conference on Information Science, Parallel and Distributed Systems (ISPDS)
abstract: Precise individual localization in densely crowded scenes remains a formidable challenge due to the complex interplay of occlusions and variable density patterns. Traditional approaches to crowd localization often employ CNNs to regress density maps, yet these are prone to inaccuracies due to the severe overlaps characteristic of dense populations. Addressing this conundrum, this paper introduces the Pyramid Focal Inverse Distance Transformer (PFIDT), a framework that leverages the multi-scale global receptive fields of Pyramid Vision Transformers to effectively conform to the multi-scale nature of crowds, thereby enhancing the precision of individual localization. The PFIDT incorporates Focal Inverse Distance techniques to adeptly tackle issues of scale variation and dense overlaps, prioritizing local small-scale features within the contextual understanding of the scene. Furthermore, the model introduces an independent Structural Similarity Index (I-SSIM) loss, encouraging the learning of local structural information and better recognition of local maxima. Rigorous testing on standard benchmarks, including the challenging ShanghaiTech dataset, has confirmed the supremacy of our method. The PFIDT has achieved outstanding results on the ShanghaiTech dataset, with Mean Absolute Errors (MAE) of 53.4 and 6.5 and Mean Squared Errors (MSE) of 93.5 and 10.7 for Parts A and B.

articleTitle: Monitoring and Optimization of Railway Switch Machine Based on Big Data Technology
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Conference on Information Science, Parallel and Distributed Systems (ISPDS)
abstract: The purpose of this paper is to discuss the application of big data technology in the monitoring and optimization of railway switch machines, and to sort out the current research status and development trends in related fields. It provides strong support for the intelligence, safety and sustainable development of the railway transportation system, and provides a useful reference for academic research and engineering practice in related fields.

articleTitle: Enhancing Both Generalization and Personalization in Personalized Federated Learning via Global and Local Knowledge Distillation
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Conference on Information Science, Parallel and Distributed Systems (ISPDS)
abstract: Federated Learning (FL) is a distributed machine learning framework that incorporates privacy protection. Under the coordination of a central server, clients collaboratively train a global model without exposing their raw data. A significant challenge in traditional FL is data heterogeneity, which can degrade the performance of the global model. To address this issue, Personalized Federated Learning (PFL) allows each client to train a personalized model that better fits the local data distribution while maintaining generalization. Many current PFL methods derive personalized models based on the global model. However, we observe that traditional training paradigms often lead to frequent forgetting of both global and personalized knowledge, impairing the personalized model’s ability to learn both generalized and client-specific knowledge. To solve this problem, we propose a new PFL framework called FedGLKD. In the training process of personalized models, FedGLKD distills knowledge from both the global model and the personalized model from the previous round. To better balance the learning of these two types of knowledge, different from traditional methods that perform knowledge distillation on the entire dataset, we introduce a novel category-wise distillation method. Specifically, when the personalized model learns data from each category, it selects the model that excels in that category as the teacher model. Our experiments on multiple datasets and various data heterogeneity scenarios demonstrate that FedGLKD outperforms state-of-the-art methods.

articleTitle: Electricity Price Prediction Based on QPSO-CNN-LSTM in the Spot Market Environment
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Conference on Information Science, Parallel and Distributed Systems (ISPDS)
abstract: The important feature of the electricity spot market is that prices fluctuate over time, and markets with a large proportion of renewable energy have more severe fluctuations in spot prices. In order to improve the accuracy of electricity price prediction during peak and valley periods, this paper proposes a price prediction method based on QPSO-CNN-LSTM. Firstly, based on the basic principles of LSTM neural network and QPSO algorithm, Convolutional Neural Networks (CNN) are used to extract features and reduce dimensionality from the dataset. Then, QPSO algorithm is used to search for the optimal parameter configuration and possible network architecture changes in LSTM network, optimize the input data in Long Short Term Memory (LSTM) neural network, and improve the prediction accuracy and training speed of LSTM network. A QPSO-CNN-LSTM load electricity price prediction model is established. A case study was conducted on the measured data of a certain electricity market in a certain region, and the proposed method was compared with other algorithms to verify its higher prediction accuracy and computational efficiency.

articleTitle: Design of UAV Obstacle Avoidance Navigation Based on LiDAR Cartographer Mapping
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Conference on Information Science, Parallel and Distributed Systems (ISPDS)
abstract: During the target tracking process, UAVs may encounter obstacles or obstructions. In order to achieve better tracking results, UAVs are required to have the ability to avoid obstacles and independently plan routes during target tracking. In this study, in the case of weak indoor satellite signals, a camera was used for visual positioning and height determination, and a LiDAR fused camera vision was used to map the surrounding environment. The relative distance and angle of obstacles were calculated, and then the autonomous obstacle avoidance navigation of the drone was completed based on path planning algorithms.

articleTitle: Application and Exploration of Computer Technology in Digital Protection of Bashu Intangible Cultural Heritage
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Conference on Information Science, Parallel and Distributed Systems (ISPDS)
abstract: This article aims to explore the application of computer technology in the digital protection of Bashu ICH. By constructing a digital protection model, and using the simulation experiment method to verify its effect. The results show that the running time of the model is short, the resource consumption is low, and the stability of the model is tested under the condition of large data storage. Furthermore, a high score means that the system has done a good job in user experience and can meet user expectations. Generally speaking, the model is efficient and practical in data collection, processing, storage and display, which significantly improves the protection level of ICH. This study not only provides a new technical means for the protection of cultural heritage in Bashu area, but also provides a useful reference for the protection of ICH around the world. Through advanced technical means, we can better inherit and carry forward valuable cultural heritage, so that more people can understand and appreciate the charm of these cultural treasures.

articleTitle: Research on Fault Warning Technology of Optical Network Based on Recurrent Neural Network
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Conference on Information Science, Parallel and Distributed Systems (ISPDS)
abstract: With the rapid development of cyber information system construction, optical networks, as a crucial component of the cyber information infrastructure, carry an increasing amount of data information and directly determine the performance of the network information system. The occurrence of faults in optical networks can severely impact various information transmissions; hence, fault warning and analysis are essential to ensure the stable and reliable operation of optical networks. Traditional fault warning and analysis of optical networks mainly rely on expert experience and network management system alarms, which have limitations such as long training cycles for backbone personnel, poor fault tolerance of network management systems, and long cycles for knowledge base construction. These limitations make it difficult to provide early warnings before faults occur in optical transmission networks, and the implementation of intelligent operation and maintenance of optical networks is challenging. Therefore, warning of optical network performance helps to accurately detect hidden dangers and determine fault causes before faults occur in optical transmission networks, and to prepare spare boards, fiber cores, and backbone forces in advance, minimizing repair time and achieving "zero" fault perception for users. This paper proposes an optical network fault warning model based on recurrent neural networks to achieve high-accuracy and intelligent response for optical network fault warnings.

articleTitle: Distributed Training Optimization for DCU
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Conference on Information Science, Parallel and Distributed Systems (ISPDS)
abstract: With the continuous advancement of large-scale models and expanding volumes of data, a single acceleration hardware is no longer sufficient to meet the training demands. Simply stacking multiple acceleration hardware together in parallel does not enhance training efficiency, but rather results in a waste of computing resources. Therefore, for existing distributed training parallel methods, we first establish the definition of parallel strategies and construct cost boundaries to enable the automatic selection of efficient parallel strategies. Additionally, we implement a time-balanced partition algorithm based on pipeline parallelism to achieve more equitable model partitioning at each stage and reduce the overall cost of model training time. Experiments conducted on a single machine with four DCU cards and a dual machine with eight DCU cards demonstrate that multiple models, supported by the automatic parallel strategy, exhibit outstanding distributed training performance. Simultaneously, the average acceleration ratio can reach 1.13× with pipeline optimization. In summary, automatic selection of strategies and pipeline parallelism optimization significantly enhances the efficiency of distributed training for large models.

articleTitle: Design and Implementation of Adaptive Resource Placement Component Based on Storm
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Conference on Information Science, Parallel and Distributed Systems (ISPDS)
abstract: In Storm systems, an efficient resource placement strategy is key to ensure application performance. However, the Storm platform uses a polled resource placement strategy, which leads to large resource and communication overheads. To solve this problem, we design and implement a Storm-based Adaptive Resource Placement Assembly (ARPA) that can dynamically adjust the placement of resources based on the real-time state and load of the system to minimise resource overhead and communication overhead. We tested the performance of APRA on a real streaming dataset. Compared with other traditional strategies, ARPA has significant advantages in terms of communication cost and number of resources used.

articleTitle: Lightweight YOLOv5s Algorithm for High-Altitude Power Operation Safety Belt Detection Based on Partial Convolution
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Conference on Information Science, Parallel and Distributed Systems (ISPDS)
abstract: To reduce the risk of accidental incidents, safety protection in high-altitude power operations is crucial. Addressing the issues of poor timeliness and lack of scenario-specific detection in existing safety harness detection methods, we propose a lightweight algorithm for detecting safety harnesses in high-altitude power operations. First, we introduce the YOLOv5s object detection model and replace its backbone with the latest FasterNet. This reduces the number of parameters while maintaining recognition accuracy and improving inference speed. Second, we replace the C3 module with the C3_Faster Block, which reduces the number of parameters and better learns the features of safety harnesses. Finally, to address the class imbalance problem in object detection, we improve the loss function by using Focal_EIoU. Experimental results on public datasets show that the proposed improvements increase the mAP value on the test set by 1.2%, improve recognition speed by 13.6%, and reduce the number of floating-point operations by 29.6%, significantly reducing computational load while enhancing recognition accuracy.

articleTitle: A Simulation Method for Industrial Control Honeynet Based on Time Series Prediction
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Conference on Information Science, Parallel and Distributed Systems (ISPDS)
abstract: This paper proposes a time series prediction based industrial control honey network simulation method to address the issue that many current industrial control honey network solutions only consider the response interaction simulation of attackers within a certain period of time and cannot effectively achieve communication simulation and collaborative work between honeypots. Firstly, the deployment and basic interaction simulation of the industrial control honeynet have been achieved; Then, a communication simulation method between devices within the industrial control honey network was studied and implemented to simulate collaborative work scenarios between devices; Secondly, using time series prediction algorithms to generate simulation data for various devices within the industrial control honey network, improving the sustained response capability of the industrial control honey network; Finally, comparative experiments have shown that the method proposed in this article can improve the ability to trap attackers, provide more data for security analysis, and help users establish a comprehensive industrial control network security protection system.

articleTitle: Research on Near-Infrared Spectroscopy Calibration Transfer Algorithm Based on Piecewise Direct Standardization and K-Nearest Neighbor
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Conference on Information Science, Parallel and Distributed Systems (ISPDS)
abstract: To address the issue of sharing qualitative models between different near-infrared spectrometers, this study explores the effectiveness of calibration transfer techniques. Two different types of near-infrared spectrometers were used as master and slave instruments to collect spectral data of samples. After preprocessing the spectral data using Savitzky-Golay (SG) smoothing and Multiplicative Scatter Correction (MSC), the study innovatively applied linear interpolation and Piecewise Direct Standardization (PDS) methods to achieve calibration Transfer. The calibration transfer effect was evaluated by calculating the Euclidean distance between the master and slave spectral data and the recognition rate of the K-Nearest Neighbor (KNN) classification model established on the master instrument. The results showed that the proposed calibration transfer method significantly improved the similarity between the master and slave spectral data, reducing the Euclidean distance from 8.6 to 0.2 and increasing the spectral recognition rate by 65.2%, approaching the recognition performance of the master instrument. This study effectively enables the sharing of qualitative recognition models between different types of near-infrared spectrometers using calibration transfer techniques, broadening the application scope of laboratory spectrometer qualitative models and providing new solutions for related fields with broad application prospects.

articleTitle: Ensembling Temporal Convolutional Networks for Heart Sound Classification
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Conference on Information Science, Parallel and Distributed Systems (ISPDS)
abstract: Accurately classifying heart sound signals is crucial for the detection and diagnosis of cardiovascular diseases. Due to the inherent complexity of heart sounds and variations among subjects, capturing the latent high-order temporal and spatial dependencies in the signals remains challenging. To this end, we design an end-to-end ensembled temporal convolutional networks aimed at enhancing accuracy. Specifically, we first use temporal convolutional networks with different dilation bases to better analyze heart sound signals and to obtain individual classifiers. Afterwards, the classifiers and a combining strategy are jointly optimized with the mixture of experts. Finally, comparative experiments regarding accuracy and F1 on three public datasets are conducted. Results show that the proposed model outperforms its components and majority voting-based ensemble model.

articleTitle: Research on Large-Area Power Grid Load Forecasting Model under Major Weather Events
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Conference on Information Science, Parallel and Distributed Systems (ISPDS)
abstract: To improve the accuracy of load forecasting for large-area power grids during major weather events, a method for predicting the load variation rate of large-area power grids based on major weather events is proposed. This method uses major meteorological disaster warning information as the identification criteria for major weather events. It constructs a sample set consisting of the month, major weather events, and the previous day's load. By converting sample rows into graphical forms, a training graph set is formed. Utilizing the graphic recognition and classification capabilities of a Convolutional Neural Network (CNN), a model for predicting the load variation rate of large-area power grids is established. Experiments conducted using this method in a large power grid company indicate that the proposed prediction method achieves higher accuracy compared to traditional manual correction methods, random forest models, and naive Bayes models.

articleTitle: Enhancing Network Security: Machine Learning Evaluation for Intrusion Detection in Power Load Management System
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Conference on Information Science, Parallel and Distributed Systems (ISPDS)
abstract: In the era of increasingly sophisticated cyber threats, ensuring the security of critical infrastructure such as power load management system is paramount. This paper presents a comprehensive evaluation of machine learning techniques for network intrusion detection within a simulated power load management environment. The dataset used in this study was created to mimic a real-world power load management system, subjected to various attacks. Each TCP/IP connection within the dataset is characterized by 41 features, both quantitative and qualitative, and is labeled as either normal or anomalous.We employed three machine learning models including Logistic Regression, Random Forest, and K-Nearest Neighbors— to analyze the dataset. By comparing the performance of these models in terms of accuracy, precision, recall, and F1 score, we identified the most effective approach for detecting anomalies in this context. Our findings provide a robust framework for enhancing network security in power load management system. This study contributes to the development of more resilient and secure power management infrastructures by leveraging advanced machine learning techniques.

articleTitle: Edge-Cloud Co-Evolutionary Task Offloading for Faulty Edge Microservices
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Conference on Information Science, Parallel and Distributed Systems (ISPDS)
abstract: Edge microservices encounter failures that affect the stability and availability of the entire edge microservice system. Some studies are devoted to developing efficient edge-edge offloading methods that offload faulty microservices' computing tasks to other healthy microservices. However, in the face of a large-scale microservice failure, it may become necessary to temporarily solicit assistance from the edge microservices of different regions, which complicates the offloading optimization problem and poses additional challenges to its efficient resolution. Therefore, this paper proposes an edge-cloud collaborative task offloading optimization model for faulty edge microservices to minimize task offloading delay and designs an edge-cloud twostage task offloading algorithm based on the WOSCA algorithm. The example results show that compared with the cloud-based offloading method, the edge-cloud collaborative offloading effectively reduces the task offloading delay by an average of 7.94%, ensuring the reliability of the edge microservice system.

articleTitle: Evaluation Method of User Terminal and Control Loop Operation Quality for New Load Management System
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Conference on Information Science, Parallel and Distributed Systems (ISPDS)
abstract: This paper proposes a new load management system oriented user-side terminal and control loop job quality evaluation method, established five indicators of availability, modifiability, reliability, security, ease of use, through a comprehensive evaluation of the user-side terminal and control loop job quality. It can find and solve the problems existing in the operation of the user terminal and the control loop in time, improve the operation efficiency and reliability of the new load management system, and provide strong support for the stable operation of the power system and the efficient use of energy.

articleTitle: CPGA-BOT: A Customized Power Grid Assistant chatBOT Fine-Tuning in Large Language Model
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Conference on Information Science, Parallel and Distributed Systems (ISPDS)
abstract: Based on Large Language Models (LLMs), AI chatbots are widely utilized in people's daily life. However, deploying general LLMs directly into domain-specific intelligent chatbots poses challenges due to their lack of training on domain-specific datasets, hindering the ability to effectively play roles within particular domains. Taking the Power Grid (the State Grid Corporation of China, SGCC) domain as an example, existing AI chatbots based on LLMs often struggle with explanations of Power Grid domain-specific terminology and providing unsatisfied responses during interactions concerning Power Grid related inquiries. Addressing these two problems, we propose a novel approach, a customized AI chatbot named CPGA-BOT that customized for Power Grid services. We collect domain-specific datasets that encompasses Power Grid related terminology and residential electricity consultation services, conducts training and fine-tuning on various LLMs. By comparing and evaluating the fine-tuned models with the native, unfine-tuned models, we observe a significant enhancement in accuracy concerning Power Grid-domain knowledge question-answering and notable improvements over the native LLMs.

articleTitle: Smart Farm Picking and Distribution Integration : Discrete Artificial Bee Colony Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Conference on Information Science, Parallel and Distributed Systems (ISPDS)
abstract: With the development of agricultural intelligence, the efficiency of picking and transportation of agricultural products directly affects the income of agricultural products. This paper proposes an integrated scheduling problem of scheduling picking robots and planning distribution vehicle routing to improve the production efficiency of agricultural products. With the objective of minimizing total cost, an efficient discrete artificial bee colony algorithm (DABC) is designed. In the scheduling phase of picking robots, the picking tasks are assigned to agricultural robots, and then an optimal path is found for each agricultural robot to complete its assigned tasks. In the vehicle route planning phase, the delivery tasks are assigned to vehicles and sorted to find the optimal route. Based on the characteristics of the problem, an integer encoding method is first used, and a high-quality and diverse initial population is generated using the nearest neighbor heuristic algorithm. Neighbor-hood operators and diversified local search opera-tors are introduced to prevent the algorithm from getting stuck in local optima. Experimental results demonstrate that the improved discrete artificial bee colony algorithm performs better.

articleTitle: Frequency Hopping Modulation Format Recognition Based on Higher-Order Cyclic Cumulants and Neural Network Classifier
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Conference on Information Science, Parallel and Distributed Systems (ISPDS)
abstract: In the field of wireless communications, the recognition of frequency hopping (FH) signal modulation formats is of significant importance for the detection and analysis of anti-drone communication signals. However, existing methods for FH signal modulation have certain limitations in handling complex signal environments, especially in terms of frequency offset resistance, timing error, anti-interference capability, and generalization ability. To address these issues, this study proposes a novel method for recognizing the modulation formats of FH signals. The Tektronix real-time spectrum analyzer is used to capture the FH signals generated by the signal source in real-time, and the signals are then processed to remove the FH. Based on this, higher-order cyclic cumulants are further calculated to deeply analyze the statistical characteristics of the signals. Finally, with the aid of a well-trained neural network classifier, precise recognition of modulation formats such as BPSK, QPSK, 8PSK, and 16QAM is achieved. This study not only improves the accuracy of FH signal recognition but also demonstrates excellent performance in resisting frequency offset and timing errors through the collection and processing of real signals. It provides a novel and efficient method for recognizing the modulation formats of FH signals in communication systems.

articleTitle: DdbiNet: A dangerous driving behavior identification network based on Resnet18
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Conference on Information Science, Parallel and Distributed Systems (ISPDS)
abstract: The direct correlation between drivers' dangerous behaviors and vehicle safety underscores the critical need for timely identification of such behaviors to enhance traffic safety. To enhance the detection of dangerous driving behaviors, we incorporated the advanced SCConv module into the ResNet18-based model, aiming to improve its accuracy. Our research revealed that the placement of the SCConv module significantly influences model accuracy. Consequently, we performed a series of ablation studies to pinpoint the optimal module placement, culminating in the formulation of the DdbiNet architecture. Concurrently, DdbiNet was benchmarked against several contemporary classification models, demonstrating superior accuracy in identifying hazardous driving behaviors. The ablation study results indicated that DdbiNet enhanced the Top1 and Top5 accuracy metrics by 29% and 31%, respectively, compared to the baseline model. The comparative analyses further affirmed that DdbiNet outperforms in the Top1 and Top5 accuracy metrics, while maintaining a lower count of parameters and FLOPs.

articleTitle: Research on Trust Evaluation Model for Vehicle-to-Grid Interaction Based on Zero Trust Architecture
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Conference on Information Science, Parallel and Distributed Systems (ISPDS)
abstract: During vehicle-to-grid (V2G) interactions, information is transmitted across multiple platforms, posing significant security risks to both information transmission and network boundaries. Traditional evaluation techniques, which rely on fixed permission assignments and predefined rules, struggle to adapt to scenarios characterized by a large number of vehicles, frequent changes in network topology, and diverse service demands. This paper proposes a trust evaluation model based on zero trust architecture. By introducing multidimensional user attribute sets, platform attribute feature sets, and user recommendation attributes, the model dynamically evaluates the trustworthiness of users and platforms. It uses trust values to dynamically authorize access subjects and assess platform reliability. This approach enhances the system's ability to identify malicious behavior and improves the security of data resources and transmission in V2G interactions. Experimental results indicate that the proposed zero trust-based trust evaluation model significantly enhances the security and dynamic responsiveness of V2G interactions.

articleTitle: Cross-border Data Security Risk Analysis and Development Suggestions of the Protection Technologies for Intelligent Connected Vehicles
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Conference on Information Science, Parallel and Distributed Systems (ISPDS)
abstract: In recent years, intelligent connected vehicles (ICVs) have developed quickly and have been progressively introduced into the international market. Nevertheless, the operation of ICVs produces a large amount of important data coming from driving vehicle and necessitating cross-border transit. As the imperfections of the regulatory framework and the infancy of protective solutions for the ICV data, these data are vulnerable to the threats like eavesdropping and tampering during cross-border transmission. The private information, especially the data barred from leaving the country, will be probably leaked to other nations, endangering individual privacy and national security. Thus, the purpose of this manuscript is to analyze the security risks of cross-border data in ICVs and provide risk mitigation strategies. The legal requirements and pertinent cross-border materials need to be sorted out firstly to establish a thorough technical process for cross-border compliance of ICV data. Additionally, the ICV data risk analyses will be performed at every stage of the cross-border process. Furthermore, some efficient risk mitigation methods need to be offered to improve the security and dependability of the across-border data of ICVs. To address the problems associated with cross-border data pertaining to ICVs, a classification method for the cross-border data of ICVs will be presented according to current rules and data categorization schemes. Finally, this manuscript provides theoretical underpinnings and useful references for building a cross-border data security protection system, as well as a thorough analysis of the development patterns of cutting-edge technologies for cross-border data.

articleTitle: Multi-feature Fusion Malicious PDF Detection Based on CBAM
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Conference on Information Science, Parallel and Distributed Systems (ISPDS)
abstract: Existing malicious PDF document detection methods often only consider single-type features, can not fully describe the features of the malicious documents, and cannot effectively detect hidden malicious content. To solve such problems, this paper proposes a malicious PDF document detection method based on Multi-feature Fusion (MF-CBAM) based on the general and structural features extracted by static analysis and API sequences extracted by dynamic analysis. At the same time, to learn more key features of malicious documents, this paper adds the convolutional block attention module to the convolutional neural network. It assigns different weights to the extracted features. Experiments using the Evasive-PDFMal2022 data set show that the model's accuracy reaches 99.85%. Compared with the model without CBAM, the accuracy of the model with CBAM is improved by 1.25 percentage points. Compared with a single-type feature detection method, it has obvious advantages in accuracy.

articleTitle: Knowledge Graph Construction Techniques for Military Intelligence
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Conference on Information Science, Parallel and Distributed Systems (ISPDS)
abstract: To construct knowledge graph for military intelligence, a set of construction methods and computing frameworks was proposed. Firstly, the storage framework and representation model of military intelligence knowledge graph are sorted out and improved. On this basis, key technologies such as automatic construction and intelligent retrieval of military intelligence knowledge graph were proposed. The constructed military intelligence knowledge graph has the ability to manage entity relationship attribute triplets, supporting automatic graph construction, fast retrieval response, and multi-modal query.

articleTitle: Deep Reinforcement Learning for Optimizing Energy Efficiency in STAR-RIS Assisted Communication Networks
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Conference on Information Science, Parallel and Distributed Systems (ISPDS)
abstract: Synchronous Transmission and Reflection Reconfigurable Intelligent Surface (STAR-RIS) is emerging as a key enhancers in future communication networks due to its low cost, minimal energy consumption, programmability, and straightforward deployment. This surface notably improve wireless network performance and optimize the energy efficiency of communication systems. A critical feature of STAR-RIS is its ability to provide extensive signal coverage and intelligently manage energy consumption through adaptive on/off switching mechanisms, thereby minimizing network power use. This paper investigates a STAR-RIS assisted communication network aimed at maximizing system energy efficiency. Owing to the fractional nature of the objective function and the complexities introduced by the intelligent switching, traditional convex optimization techniques are inadequate. Consequently, this study introduces a novel approach using deep reinforcement learning, the Twin Delayed Deep Deterministic Policy Gradient (TD3) algorithm, and proposes an enhanced variant, TCD3. Simulation results indicate significant improvements in system energy efficiency with both algorithms, with TCD3 surpassing TD3 in terms of learning speed, average rewards, and reduced variance.

Author Keywords: Twin Delayed Deep Deterministic Policy Gradient(TD3)

articleTitle: Research on Optimization Scheduling Model for the Use and Maintenance of Protective Vehicles
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Conference on Information Science, Parallel and Distributed Systems (ISPDS)
abstract: The optimization scheduling model for the use and maintenance of protective vehicles has problems such as limited research content, high degree of customization, low maintenance cycle and optimal strategy quality, and multi-objective scheduling conflicts. This article explores the importance of maintaining and optimizing protective vehicles, especially in maintaining the conflict readiness of key assets such as vehicles, in response to current issues. Two different maintenance and training balance models are analyzed, and their advantages and disadvantages are evaluated, providing feasible optimization directions. The first model is based on economies of scale, using periodic batch repairs to reduce costs, but this method may result in some vehicles being unusable due to time exhaustion during training. The second model adopts nonperiodic repair based on perfect dynamic balance, which may increase costs and management difficulties, but can ensure that the remaining time distribution of all vehicles is more reasonable, thus meeting the requirements in both training and preparation states. Both of these modes have their own applicable scenarios, and the most suitable maintenance scheduling strategy can be selected based on specific situations and needs. Ultimately, the optimization suggestions proposed in the article aim to improve the efficiency of vehicle usage while considering cost-effectiveness to support more effective training and conflict readiness.

articleTitle: Research on Dynamic Protection Technology of Network Security Spatial Data Assets Based on Neural Networks
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Conference on Information Science, Parallel and Distributed Systems (ISPDS)
abstract: With the rapid development of network technology, the security of data assets in cyberspace has become crucial. This article proposes a dynamic security detection system based on neural networks to address the shortcomings of existing protection mechanisms. This system simulates biological neural networks and integrates key functions such as identity authentication, anomaly detection, and penetration testing, aiming to achieve real-time protection of data assets. The study elaborated on the system design and explored its potential in improving network security performance. In response to the challenges of model training resource consumption, missing data labels, and vulnerability to attacks, this study proposes optimization strategies such as data augmentation, label mapping, and adversarial training, which significantly improve the robustness and accuracy of the model. Experimental verification shows that the proposed technical solution has significant advantages in anomaly detection and robustness. This study provides a new perspective for the field of network security and lays the foundation for future research and practice.

articleTitle: Emotional Fine-tuning Model for Blended Teaching
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Conference on Information Science, Parallel and Distributed Systems (ISPDS)
abstract: Existing computational methods for sentiment analysis using online comments overlook individual user characteristics, which hinders their high-quality development of blended teaching. By fine-tuning the sentiment of comments with the consideration of individual user traits, we can grasp students' genuine emotions and enhance teaching outcomes. This paper proposes a multi-feature-integrated emotion fine-tuning model that accurately captures the emotional valence of users in a blended teaching environment. Based on MOOC online comments, the model incorporates additional social factors of users. It quantifies emotion fine-tuning value by combining personality and user influence models, considering personality traits, social influence, and the impact of historical comments on emotional valence. Testing demonstrates that this approach effectively reveals learners' psychological states, validating its efficacy.

articleTitle: Research on Brain Tumor Segmentation Using a 3D U-Net with Deformable Convolution
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Conference on Information Science, Parallel and Distributed Systems (ISPDS)
abstract: In brain tumour image segmentation, due to the problems of brain tumours of different sizes and shapes, blurred boundaries as well as unbalanced categories, this paper proposes a 3D U-Net model with deformable convolutions for brain tumor segmentation (D3DC U-Net) to enhance the accuracy of brain tumor image segmentation. By incorporating deformable 3D convolutions into the basic framework of 3D U-Net, the model's ability to learn various sizes and shapes of brain tumors is effectively improved, thereby enhancing segmentation accuracy. The addition of convolutional attention mechanism in D3D U-Net enhances the network's feature extraction capability, strengthens spatial information acquisition, and enables more accurate identification of brain tumor regions. The use of a hybrid loss function alleviates the issue of brain tumor data imbalance. Extensive experiments on the BraTS2020 dataset demonstrate superior performance of the proposed network in brain tumor segmentation of MRI images compared to other medical image segmentation methods.

articleTitle: Bayesian Probability Intelligent Forecasting Model Based on Rainfall during Flood Season
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Conference on Information Science, Parallel and Distributed Systems (ISPDS)
abstract: In order to make better use of the revised ensemble probability forecast based on the information of the historical prior probability precipitation distribution function, based on the Bayesian probability decision theory, this paper used the actual rainfall data from 1981 to 2010 in Xijiang River Basin and the European ensemble forecast products from April to September in 2016 as the prior information, and established Bayes based probability prediction model for heavy rain in Xijiang River Basin to correct the European ensemble probability prediction products and to carry out the grading test. Bayesian methods are more accurate than other methods, making it easier to establish predictive models. From the results of forecasting experiments, it can be seen that the ensemble probability forecasting product modified by the Bayesian method can improve the forecasting ability of heavy rain in flood season. Except for September, the Brier scores (BS) of other months in flood season within 24-72 hours are better than those of ensemble probability forecast, and the possibility of a false heavy rain forecast can be reduced to a certain extent; there is a monthly difference in the distribution of the true skill statistic (TSS) high score areas in pre-flood season: with the increase of precipitation intensity and scope from April to June, the scores of most river basins increase. In conclusion, this work can provide a reference for forecasters to carry out the prediction of heavy rainfall in the Xiiang River Basin.

articleTitle: Research on Penetrative Security Pathways in Financial Regulation Based on Blockchain
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Conference on Information Science, Parallel and Distributed Systems (ISPDS)
abstract: Traditional models of financial regulation often need help with issues such as information asymmetry and regulatory inefficiencies. However, the inherent features of decentralization and immutability within blockchain technology present novel opportunities for enhancing regulatory practices. Through a comprehensive examination of blockchain technology's application within financial regulation, this study proposes various technical pathways to achieve regulatory penetrability. Specifically, the paper defines mathematical models for four distinct modes: negotiated regulation, embedded regulation, automated regulation, and dynamic regulation, all implemented using Python. Moreover, this research emphasizes the critical role of establishing appropriate regulatory frameworks to facilitate realizing these goals. Doing so aims to advance the evolution and enhancement of financial regulatory models, ultimately fostering the stable development of financial markets. Additionally, the experimental methodologies and results analysis are integrated into the study, providing empirical insights into the efficacy of the proposed approaches.

articleTitle: Design and Application of Artificial Intelligence-Based Sports Rehabilitation Robot Auxiliary System
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Conference on Information Science, Parallel and Distributed Systems (ISPDS)
abstract: With the development of artificial intelligence technology, the field of sports rehabilitation has also made significant progress. Our team adopted the moving human body target recognition technology to achieve "human motion capture", "exercise prescription", "exercise rehabilitation", and the application of "combination of physical medicine", and the use of "OMO" mode to achieve the effective aggregation of online, mobile and offline, to create an online-mobile-offline integrated health exercise prescription design system. Through precise mechanical structure, control system and sensor system, and real-time data monitoring, the system provides personalized rehabilitation training program, which is suitable for neurological rehabilitation, orthopedic rehabilitation and elderly rehabilitation and other scenarios. Its advantage is that it can adjust the training plan according to the specific situation of the patient, feedback the movement status in real time, improve the accuracy and safety of the training, and continuously optimize the rehabilitation program through data-driven.

articleTitle: KPCA for Open Source Security: Analyzing and Assessing Component Vulnerabilities
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Conference on Information Science, Parallel and Distributed Systems (ISPDS)
abstract: The widespread use of open source components in software development presents significant security risks due to complex dependencies and frequent vulnerabilities. Current security tools often struggle with high false positives and miss critical vulnerabilities. This paper introduces a new Kernel Principal Component Analysis (KPCA)-based method to enhance the detection and security assessment of these components. Our approach leverages advanced feature extraction through KPCA, significantly improving the accuracy of vulnerability detection over traditional methods. We demonstrate the superiority of our method through comparative experiments, highlighting its potential to contribute to safer software development practices.

articleTitle: Innovative Application of Deep Learning and Large Model
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Conference on Information Science, Parallel and Distributed Systems (ISPDS)
abstract: With the growth of computing power and data volume, deep learning and large-scale models are widely used in AI fields. Large-scale pre-trained models like the transformer architecture are the preferred solution for downstream tasks. This study explores how they drive innovation in intelligent applications. By constructing deep neural networks with hundreds of millions of parameters and using data sets and optimization technology, new methods and applications are proposed in image recognition, text generation, speech recognition. Especially, a new large-scale model adjustment strategy is designed, which effectively improves model generalization and adaptability. Experiments show significant performance improvement.

articleTitle: Research on the Application of Natural Language Processing Technology in Medicine Patent Retrieval
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Conference on Information Science, Parallel and Distributed Systems (ISPDS)
abstract: In view of the high professionalism and complexity of medicine patent text, traditional patent retrieval mainly relies on manual operation and simple text Processing methods, this paper aims to use Natural Language Processing (NLP) technology to efficiently obtain valuable information in medicine patent retrieval. To transform unstructured text into meaningful information. Through in-depth research on the characteristics and structure of medicine patent text, a new structured feature extraction algorithm of patent text is proposed, and a patent retrieval system based on NLP is developed, which can carry out instant structured processing, and can automatically identify and translate text into corresponding patented medicines, and nearly 300 medicine patent abstracts are tested by experiment. The system performance is good. The system achieves the expected effect.

articleTitle: Audio Feature Extraction Algorithms and Implementation Technologies Analysis
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Conference on Information Science, Parallel and Distributed Systems (ISPDS)
abstract: LIBROSA is a powerful Python audio data processing library introduced in recent years. Based on LIBROSA provided source codes, two types of feature data extraction algorithms are analyzed in detail, including MEL power spectrum and CHROMA syllable spectrums. By each algorithm, 128, 12 floating point numbers are extracted as the feature data of their corresponding spectrums. In addition, from multi perspectives of basic music theory, mathematical analysis, signal processing, computer programming and so on, deeply discusses LIBROSA library functions involved Discrete Fourier Transform (DFT), Triangular filter, Gaussian filter, and other programming technologies. The DFT algorithm, time domain window function, syllable feature data extraction, band-pass filter code analysis and other contents discussed have important reference value in data processing, deep learning and other fields of underlying model creation, source codes development and so on

articleTitle: Verifiable Federated Learning Based on Data Service Quality
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Conference on Information Science, Parallel and Distributed Systems (ISPDS)
abstract: In traditional distributed system, the central server has absolute management authority over data, while in federated learning, data is provided by task execution nodes, and the central node has no direct viewing authority. Task execution nodes provide data for local model training in a distributed manner, and the global model plays the role of aggregation of these local models. The quality of the global model is affected by the local models provided by task execution nodes, which are generated by algorithms and data. To measure the impact of data on the model, the concept of data service quality is introduced, which is defined as the accuracy, completeness, and relevance of the data to the task. High-quality data provides more reliable model updates, while low-quality data can cause model degradation. At the same time, the task node data service quality can be divided into malicious and non-malicious. Non-malicious behavior may be caused by data collection errors, while malicious behavior such as data poisoning may destroy the global model. A method for evaluating data service quality, node contribution, and credibility is designed to select high-quality nodes to participate in federated learning tasks. A large number of experiments were conducted on the public data set CIFAR-10, which verified the feasibility and superiority of VFL-DSQM.

articleTitle: The Design and Realization of Intelligent Question Answering Technology in Military Field
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Conference on Information Science, Parallel and Distributed Systems (ISPDS)
