abstract: Intelligent question answering technology is one of the most concerned and widely used research directions in the field of Artificial Intelligence. With the accumulation of massive data, traditional search and query methods cannot meet the military needs for rapid acquisition of high-value information and knowledge. The application of intelligent question answering technology in the current military field lack the real-time accuracy, context understanding, and adaptability needed for dynamic combat situations. For the duty professional work, this paper conducts research on intelligent question answering technology based on duty data. We propose a method for knowledge graph construction and answer retrieval matching technology. Our method integrates and extracts the entities, relationships, and attributes information from the multi-source heterogeneous duty data, which builds the knowledge graph. Based on the knowledge graph, the intelligent question answering for duty achieves more accurate answers by making use of the question analysis and intelligent matching technology. By integrating artificial intelligence technology into the command information system, the intelligence level can be effectively improved to support the competition for the core intellectual power in military field.

articleTitle: A Strategy-Proof Combinatorial Double Auction Mechanism for Cloud Resource Allocation
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Conference on Information Science, Parallel and Distributed Systems (ISPDS)
abstract: The resource allocation optimization problem based on combination auctions, in which cloud service providers provide multiple types of resources and cloud users request different combinations of resources, is still a challenge in cloud computing and edge computing. The diversity of demands and the complexity of resource combinations make the direct search for optimal solutions extremely difficult, and the mechanism design in the combination double auction scenario also faces more challenges. We propose a strategy-proof combinatorial double auction mechanism for cloud resource allocation (CBAA) model, which utilizes a greedy mechanism to solve the dynamic allocation of multidimensional cloud resources and designs a payment algorithm based on critical value theory, which ensures the truthfulness of all the participants and encourages the bidders to offer their prices in a truthful manner. This mechanism takes into account the utility of the cloud user and the cloud service provider and maximizes social welfare. The experimental results show that compared to other algorithms, CBAA improves social welfare by approximately 17%-20%, the utility of cloud users and cloud service providers by approximately 4.09%, and the cloud service provider's resource utilization by approximately 10%. The CBAA is shown to be incentive compatible and individually rational and to achieve budget equilibrium and economic efficiency.

articleTitle: An Improved Artificial Bee Colony Algorithm Based on k-means Clustering
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Conference on Information Science, Parallel and Distributed Systems (ISPDS)
abstract: The Artificial Bee Colony (ABC) algorithm is a simple and efficient optimization method with few control parameters and robust global search capabilities. It performs well in solving complex optimization problems but has weak local search abilities and a tendency to fall into local optima. To address these issues, we propose an improved Artificial Bee Colony algorithm based on k-means clustering (IKABC). The IKABC algorithm enhances local search and convergence abilities by utilizing k-means clustering to divide the population and optimize the search process. Additionally, a search strategy that balances global optimization and local search is introduced, alongside an improved roulette wheel selection strategy, to make nectar source searches more directional and to balance the algorithm's exploration and exploitation capabilities. Finally, the IKABC algorithm is compared through simulations with other enhanced ABC algorithms using 12 benchmark test functions, demonstrating its superior performance in solving complex optimization problems.

articleTitle: A Electric Vehicle Reducer Bearing Fault Diagnosis Method Based on Space-Time Aware Convolution and Transformer Structure
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Conference on Information Science, Parallel and Distributed Systems (ISPDS)
abstract: The reliability and efficiency of industrial machinery are critically dependent on the early detection of faults in critical components such as reducer bearings. This paper presents a novel approach to fault diagnosis method in reducer bearings that leverages the power of space-time aware convolution and the Transformer structure. The proposed method integrates the temporal dynamics and spatial features of the bearing vibrations to enhance the fault detection process. Our approach begins with the acquisition of vibration signals from the electric vehicle reducer bearings. These signals are then processed using a space-time aware convolutional neural network (ST-CNN) that is designed to capture both the spatial patterns and the temporal evolution of the signals. The ST-CNN is followed by a Transformer-based model that further refines the fault detection by attending to the most relevant features in the sequence of processed signals. We have conducted extensive experiments on a dataset comprising various fault types and severities. The results demonstrate that our method outperforms traditional fault detection techniques, including those based solely on CNNs or LSTMs. Our model achieved an accuracy of 92.4% on the self-built data set, far exceeding other comparison models.

articleTitle: Research and Suggestions for Evaluation Metrics of On-board Video Desensitization
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Conference on Information Science, Parallel and Distributed Systems (ISPDS)
abstract: Sensitive data leakage has become an urgent problem to be solved as more images based functionalities are being developed in vehicles. However, there is a scarcity of evaluation for on-board videos data desensitization. This research analyzes on-board video desensitization process including the image pre-processing stage, sensitive area localization stage and sensitive area desensitization stage. Considering that, this paper presents several evaluation methods and metrics of sensitive target detection performance, privacy-utility evaluation of video file metadata and image, so as to provide reference for the related research on the desensitization evaluation of on-board video.

articleTitle: Advanced Battery Defect Detection Using VisionMaster: A Deep Learning Approach to Enhance Accuracy and Efficiency
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Conference on Information Science, Parallel and Distributed Systems (ISPDS)
abstract: VisionMaster algorithm development platform is a powerful machine vision software. The platform aims to provide users with efficient and convenient algorithm tools to quickly build visual applications and solve complex visual detection challenges, further promoting the deep application and development of machine vision technology. In this study, the process of battery defect detection utilizing the VisionMaster algorithm platform is thoroughly examined. The detection workflow is initiated by acquiring 2D color images of batteries, followed by the collection of 3D depth maps. These imaging modalities are integrated to provide a comprehensive assessment of battery quality. The VisionMaster platform's embedded vision algorithms are discussed in detail, highlighting their role in the quality evaluation process. The visualization of the scanning process, the interpretation of feedback from the vision system, and the corresponding responses from the lower-level control systems are described.Results from both 2D and 3D camera scans are analyzed to illustrate the advantages and limitations of each method. The study demonstrates the core value of the vision detection system in ensuring quality control in battery manufacturing. The integration of VisionMaster with advanced vision algorithms is shown to significantly enhance the accuracy and reliability of defect detection, thereby improving overall production quality.

articleTitle: Heterogeneous Network Embedding Method Based on Hyperbolic Space
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Conference on Information Science, Parallel and Distributed Systems (ISPDS)
abstract: The core of heterogeneous network embedding is to transform nodes and edges into low and dense vector representations while preserving the structural features and semantic information of the original network. The existing embedding methods based on European space can not store the hierarchical structure of the network, nor can capture the rich semantic information contained in the heterogeneous network. To improve the embedding quality of heterogeneous networks and reduce information loss, a hyperbolic space-based embedding method for heterogeneous networks is proposed. Firstly, a random walk guided by meta-path is used to obtain the node neighborhood information and semantic relation of the network. Then the heterogeneous network is embedded into hyperbolic space based on Poincare sphere model, and the Riemann stochastic gradient descent method is used to optimize the model. Experiments on multiple datasets show that the proposed method has better performance than other baseline methods, and preserves more complete network information with fewer dimensions of storage space.

articleTitle: PR-Graph2vec: PageRank-based Graph Embedding Algorithm for Phishing Detection in the Ethereum Network
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Conference on Information Science, Parallel and Distributed Systems (ISPDS)
abstract: Ethereum, as one of today's most active blockchain platforms, provides extensive data for academic interest, thanks to its transparency and has garnered broad academic interest. Many studies model Ethereum transaction records as graph structures and design models to analyze phishing address transaction features. However, they often neglect the deep network structure of transaction sub-calls and lack efficient random walk strategies for optimal subgraph sampling. Therefore, this study introduces PR-Graph2vec, a PageRank- based graph embedding algorithm that captures the topological features of network phishing attacks from both the contract and sub-call perspectives, thereby improving phishing address detection. We extracted all transactions labeled as phishing from the blockchain explorer EtherScan to build a transaction network graph. Then, by aggregating the features of transaction call types and account types, we performed in-depth feature mining on transaction sub-calls. Finally, we used PageRank for biased sampling, significantly reducing the graph size. Experimental results demonstrate that our proposed Ethereum phishing detection model, PR-Graph2vec, excels in practical applications, achieving 91.0% precision and an 86.9% F1-score.

articleTitle: Blockchain-based Federated Learning Data Sharing Model
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Conference on Information Science, Parallel and Distributed Systems (ISPDS)
abstract: Federated learning has been widely researched and applied in various scenarios. In the context of mobile computing, federated learning protects users from exposing their private data while enabling collaborative training of global models for various practical applications. However, the security of federated learning has come under increasing scrutiny due to attacks from malicious clients or untrusted central servers on global models or user privacy data. To address these security concerns, this paper proposes a federated learning data sharing model based on blockchain and reputation values. This data sharing model utilizes IPFS for storing model parameters, with the model parameters stored in IPFS hash addresses to alleviate the storage pressure on the blockchain. Additionally, an access control mechanism is designed. A consensus mechanism based on reputation values is proposed, aiming to enhance model performance in the face of malicious attacks.

articleTitle: Research on Change Detection Algorithms for Image Interaction and Edge Enhancement
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Conference on Information Science, Parallel and Distributed Systems (ISPDS)
abstract: Most of the existing detection methods ignore the spatial and temporal characteristics of the two images and global dependence of the interconnections, resulting in many irrelevant changes (such as illumination, the atmosphere, seasonal changes in vegetation) to produce the phenomenon of misdetection; at the same time, the existing methods of change detection. Meanwhile, the existing change detection methods are not easy to obtain structural details in high-resolution remote sensing images and the detection accuracy needs to be improved. Based on the global information interaction and edge detection method of dual-time-phase image, a network model is proposed, which consists of three parts and is divided into three modules, namely, edge structure and image feature extraction, image transformer and change region discrimination. Edge detection is performed on the dual-temporal phase image to obtain the edge map, edge detection can effectively improve the edge details of the detection results, the edge map and the original image are fused for feature extraction, and the extracted dual-temporal phase features are sent to the image transformer BIT for global spatial-temporal modeling to establish the connection, modeling the remote context in the dual-temporal image in an efficient and effective way, and finally through the simple region of change discriminative module for discrimination obtaining the detection results. The algorithm achieves 96.2% F1 on CDD dataset and 93.8% F1 on BCDD dataset, which is superior with better stability and robustness compared with some known algorithms.

articleTitle: A Robust Visual Localization Method with 4 DOF in the Case of Planar Motion
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Conference on Information Science, Parallel and Distributed Systems (ISPDS)
abstract: As robotics technology advances rapidly, robots are being extensively utilized in a variety of areas including warehouse inspection, logistics handling, and smart homes. However, in methods utilizing 2D image databases for visual localization, factors such as dynamic object interference, changes in lighting conditions, and environments with low texture lead to high errors in image feature matching points and sparse matching points, thereby reducing the success rate of localization. To tackle this problem, this study introduces a robust visual localization method for planar motion scenarios. Unlike existing approaches that focus solely on rotation around the Y-axis, this method accounts for rotations around both the X-axis and the Y-axis. By incorporating motion constraints, it optimizes the estimation of the essential matrix and the triangulation process. This reduces the need for 2D-2D feature matching points between query images and reference images in the database, thereby enhancing the robustness of the localization method. Finally, the proposed method demonstrates higher localization accuracy, robustness, and success rate in both simulation experiments and publicly available real-world localization datasets. This provides a significant approach for addressing the localization challenges of planar motion robots.

articleTitle: Blockchain-based Federated Learning System for Intelligent Traffic Management
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Conference on Information Science, Parallel and Distributed Systems (ISPDS)
abstract: In response to the statistical heterogeneity, data sharing and privacy protection issues faced by the Internet of Vehicles in intelligent traffic field, this paper proposes a blockchain-based federated learning system for intelligent traffic management. This system employs a federated learning algorithm that leverages server-side momentum gradient descent and proximal term optimization to accelerate the convergence rate of the model while reducing the negative impact of statistical heterogeneity on model accuracy. Additionally, this system utilizes blockchain as a trusted third party to verify local model updates of vehicles through smart contracts, ensuring the credibility of local model updates. The global models are evaluated by the intelligent traffic management center, and then stored in the Inter-Planetary File System, with model addresses uploaded to blockchain, which ensures model data privacy and reduces system storage pressure. The experimental results show that the performance of our system’s algorithm on MNIST and CIFAR-10 datasets under different degrees of heterogeneity conditions surpasses that of baseline algorithms. It is capable of training high-availability models in heterogeneous Internet of Vehicles scenarios.

articleTitle: Design and Application of Adaptive Image Recognition Algorithm Based on Deep Reinforcement Learning
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Conference on Information Science, Parallel and Distributed Systems (ISPDS)
abstract: Image recognition technology is widely used in fields such as intelligent video analysis, but neural network models often suffer from weak generalization capabilities. To address this challenge, this study proposes an adaptive recognition strategy based on deep reinforcement learning. Firstly, a convolutional neural network that combines the features of ResNet and DenseNet is designed to ensure feature representation capability while improving computational efficiency. Secondly, an adaptive data augmentation mechanism is designed based on online feedback to dynamically adjust image transformation methods and intensity, actively adapting to changes in input distribution patterns. Thirdly, an online update framework based on incremental learning is constructed, using a small amount of new data to continue training the model, enabling continuous knowledge absorption and capability improvement. Finally, through image classification experiments, it is demonstrated that this strategy improves recognition accuracy by more than 5% compared to baseline models, especially demonstrating robustness in transfer learning and adaptation to new environments, laying the foundation for building intelligent upgradable visual analysis systems.
